subject: Migration schedule orchestration for DataFlux PoC - coordination
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@dataflux.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 10 Jun 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Migration PoC - availability & constraints

Hi Olga, Ben —

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. We’re ready to schedule the technical deep-dive that owners on our side (infra + model ops) need to greenlight the migration from our current self-hosted inference stack. High-level asks from us:
- Validate network and egress requirements (we run behind strict NATs)
- Walk through KV cache persistence and cold-start behavior for long contexts
- Discuss rollback/fallback plan in case of throughput regressions

Stakeholders who will attend: myself (infra lead), Elaine Park (procurement, may join for calendar/contract notes), and Ravi Menon (ML infra). Our preferred window next week: Tue/Wed morning PST or Thu afternoon PST. If you have fixed slots, please propose.

Attached the network diagram for the current deployment for reference.

[Attachment: dataflux-network-diagram.png (image/png)]

Cheers,
Samir
Infrastructure Lead | DataFlux
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@dataflux.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jun 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Migration PoC - availability & constraints

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the diagram — that helps. We can cover all three asks in a focused 60–75 minute deep-dive. Proposed agenda (concise):
1) 10m intro & success criteria (DataFlux goals + rollback triggers)
2) 20m network, auth, and egress checklist (security + KMS)
3) 20m serving runtime behavior: KV cache, cold starts, batching knobs
4) 10m ops runbook and rollback playbook (who does what)
5) 5–10m open Q&A and next steps

Available slots (PST):
- Tue 2028-06-13 09:00–10:30
- Tue 2028-06-13 13:00–14:30
- Wed 2028-06-14 09:30–11:00
- Thu 2028-06-15 15:00–16:30

Marissa (solutions eng) will take the runbook and KV-cache items. Ben, can you add any commercial constraints (billing/credits) to the agenda?

I’m attaching our initial migration runbook so everyone can skim beforehand.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: migration-runbook-v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

- We can offer a short-term trial credit to cover the PoC run; I’ll follow up with an exact figure once we lock the expected token volume.
- If DataFlux needs on-prem network peering or reserved capacity during the PoC, we should know ASAP to reserve nodes.
